catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antoine-leona: A 1913 entry on Antoine-Léonard de Chézy — the first professor of Sanskrit in Europe. Arthur Remy honors his orientalist labors. His chair at the Collège was new. The East opened to French scholars. A pioneer of the Indian tongues.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-councils-of-q: This 1913 reference article on the councils of Quierzy — the Carolingian synods. Nicholas Weber notes their famous acts. The bishops judged the predestined Gottschalk. The ninth century dates their solemn decrees. The synods of the royal palace. Their 853 decrees are famed.
little-fuzzy:
H. Beam Piper opens this science fiction novel in bright sunlight. Jack Holloway squints against an orange sun over a gorge. He lifts his manipulator higher on contragravity generators. A red rag marks the blast point against the rock face.

Holloway has fired a thousand blast-shots across many planets. Even small shots still please him, he admits. His thumb sends the radio impulse that fires this one. The solitary prospector's routine will soon meet a small, furry visitor. Debris pelted the weightless manipulator as the shot fired. A thousand earlier blasts, including thermonuclears, preceded this small one.
podcast-dannyjones-SpOFsJGldzY:
Ray Connolly joins Danny Jones to tell the story billed in the episode's title. It is his time inside a doomsday cult he calls the most evil religion in history. It ends with his break from it. Connolly describes recruitment, control, and the beliefs that kept members obedient as the group's end-times clock ran.

Former-member testimony is the raw material of cult studies, and Connolly's account follows its classic shape: love at the door, fear at the center, and a hard road out. Jones asks what the group taught and what it did, letting the specifics accumulate. The group's identity and Connolly's claims rest on his word, preserved here as his testimony. Listeners interested in how total belief systems actually operate day to day will find a survivor's manual disguised as a horror story.
podcast-joerogan-1VgHCqtApzY:
Magician David Blaine joins Joe Rogan for episode 2056 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Blaine is famed for stunts of pain and grit: buried, frozen, starved, and held under water for the crowd. He sits with Rogan for a long talk.

Blaine tells how he trains his body and mind to bear what most men cannot. He shares the stunts that near broke him and why he keeps at it. Rogan, a trained fighter, meets him on the ground of pain and will. Listeners get a rare talk with a man who makes art of grit. The library keeps the episode as a record of his visit.
podcast-joerogan-6vktDo8IWzY:
Eric Weinstein's episode 1628 of the Joe Rogan Experience comes from the middle of his long run as a guest. Weinstein, a mathematician who manages money and writes on science, uses these talks to air ideas he says the academy ignores.

He and Rogan range over physics, failing institutions, and the cost of safe, career-first thinking in science. Weinstein argues that bold work gets punished while dull work gets funded. Rogan, a fan and a foil, keeps the talk moving with plain questions. For new listeners, this visit is a good sample of Weinstein's style: dense, combative, and sure of itself.
podcast-joerogan-i4dbLZTJjZY:
Egyptologist Zahi Hawass joins Joe Rogan for episode 2321 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Hawass is Egypt's best known archaeologist, famed for his digs, his TV work, and his firm views on the pyramids. He rarely gives ground to fringe claims.

Hawass and Rogan talk tombs, kings, and the true tale of how the great stones rose. Hawass bats down lost-tech claims with the calm of a man who has dug the sites for decades. Rogan presses him on the gaps that feed the fringe. Listeners get the expert case at full length. The library keeps the episode as a record of his visit.
podcast-joerogan-livgMzeO-ZY:
Billy Carson talks with Rogan for episode 2160 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Carson runs 4BiddenKnowledge, a platform teaching his reading of ancient history: alien visitors, old tablets, and knowledge hidden from the public. He is the internet's esoteric teacher, and Rogan gives him the long form.

He lays out his account of the ancient world, from Sumerian texts to Egyptian monuments, in his confident lecturer's flow. Rogan asks where the tablets end and the reading begins. The episode is a full statement of the ancient-astronaut faith in its current form, kept for the open-minded and the curious alike.
podcast-joerogan-pcCKDDa3MzY:
Former Texas governor Rick Perry and advocate W. Bryan Hubbard join Joe Rogan for episode 2251. Hubbard works to expand legal access to ibogaine, a psychedelic used to treat addiction and brain injury. Perry, once a hard-line conservative, became an unlikely backer of that cause.

The guests explain how ibogaine helped veterans with trauma and opioid addiction in early studies and clinics abroad. Perry talks about what changed his mind after hearing veterans' stories. Hubbard covers the policy fight to fund research in Texas and beyond. Rogan, a longtime psychedelics voice, helps them make the case to a broad audience.
